overview: Benin's court commissioned brass sculpture to preserve royal memory and express authority. This Edo kingdom was centered in present-day Nigeria, distinct from the modern country named Benin.

items.text: An incoming oba commissioned a commemorative head honoring his predecessor. These idealized royal images emphasize kingship rather than individual facial likeness.
Brass-casting guild artists produced rectangular plaques for the palace. A surviving example is dated approximately 1540 to 1570.
Palace courtyards and galleries included wooden pillars covered with cast brass plaques.
Scholars interpret palace plaques as an archive later consulted about court ritual and regalia.
British removal of royal works in 1897 disrupted their original contexts. Scholars therefore combine stylistic and material evidence when reconstructing their chronology.
